protections: Lease revocation and renewal requested from namespace N may only act on leases owned by N (or a namespace N legitimately administers); the lease's namespace must not be taken on trust from the caller-supplied lease ID.

evidence: vault/logical_system_paths.go:2715 pattern (leases/)?revoke + optional url_lease_id serves sys/revoke, sys/revoke/<id>, sys/leases/revoke/<id>
vault/request_handling.go:942 the namespace swap only covers exact body-form sys/leases/{lookup,renew,revoke,revoke-force}; sys/revoke and URL-id forms keep the requester namespace for the ACL check
vault/logical_system.go:2046-2061 handleRevoke passes the lease ID straight to Revoke/LazyRevoke without comparing namespaces
vault/expiration.go:2001-2012 loadEntry resolves the lease namespace from the lease-ID suffix, not from the request
vault/expiration.go:996-1009 revokeCommon revokes whatever loadEntry returned, with no namespace comparison
vault/expiration.go:923-938 lazyRevokeInternal marks the foreign lease expired, with no namespace comparison
vault/expiration.go:1237-1239 by contrast, Renew rejects ns.ID != le.namespace.ID, so revoke lacks the guard that its renew sibling has

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Prefix revocation is visibly scoped to the request namespace's lease view (expiration.go:1180), and revoke-prefix/revoke-force are sudo-only paths (logical_system.go:81-84), so the route looks both namespace-scoped and admin-only.
evidence: vault/logical_system_paths.go:2756 and :2789 sys/(leases/)?revoke-force/<prefix> and revoke-prefix/<prefix>

vault/expiration.go:1161-1171 when the prefix has no trailing slash, it is treated as a single lease ID and loaded via loadEntry, which resolves the namespace from the ID suffix (expiration.go:2001-2012), then revokeCommon/LazyRevoke run on it
vault/expiration.go:1176-1180 only the slash branch is limited to leaseView(ns)
vault/logical_system.go:81-84 sudo protects these paths but does not decide the namespace (a namespace admin holds sudo in their own namespace)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: A lease ID without a namespace suffix looks like a local or plain ID; a guard that compares the ID suffix with the request namespace ID treats an empty suffix as 'no namespace info' and lets it through.
evidence: vault/expiration.go:2001-2012 an empty nsID maps the lookup to RootNamespace, so a suffix-less ID names a root-namespace lease even when the request is from a child namespace
vault/expiration.go:1132-1134 only non-root token lease IDs carry the .nsID suffix; root-namespace IDs have none

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Putting the namespace-equality check inside the shared ExpirationManager.Revoke/revokeCommon/LazyRevoke looks like defense in depth that covers T1 and T2 at once.
evidence: vault/core.go:1981-1983 seal-time revocation of a pending-use token calls Revoke with activeContext and does not adopt the token's namespace
vault/request_handling.go:1170-1173 last-use token revocation calls LazyRevoke with the request ctx, whose namespace can be a child of the token's namespace
vault/ha.go:359 internal Revoke with activeContext
vault/expiration.go:1117 RevokeByToken uses lazyRevokeInternal on indexed leases
vault/request_handling.go:937-941 parent-namespace operators are meant to act on child-namespace leases through the body-form canonical paths (still ACL-gated)

traps.reason_to_dismiss: The comment says the operation is still gated by ACLs (request_handling.go:940-941), and the ACL is evaluated as ns.Path + req.Path in the swapped namespace (policy/acl.go:373).
evidence: vault/request_handling.go:942-958 for body-form canonical sys/leases/{renew,revoke,lookup,revoke-force}, the request namespace is replaced by the namespace named in the caller-supplied lease_id suffix before handling
vault/expiration.go:1233-1239 Renew compares the ctx namespace with le.namespace; on the swapped route both come from the same lease ID, so the check is vacuous
vault/logical_system.go:2046-2050 handleRevoke builds revokeCtx from the (swapped) ctx namespace, so a handler check modelled on Renew would be vacuous here too

conflicts.what: The natural shared-layer fix for T1/T2, a strict ns.ID == le.namespace.ID check in revokeCommon/lazyRevokeInternal (expiration.go:983/918), breaks internal token revocation that calls Revoke/LazyRevoke with activeContext or a child-namespace request ctx (core.go:1983, request_handling.go:1173, ha.go:359). The check must sit at the sys handlers, or allow internal callers through.

Removing the namespace swap at request_handling.go:942-958, or rejecting every lease whose namespace differs from the requester's, breaks parent-namespace administration of child-namespace leases, which that block exists to support.

fairness_risks: A parent or root namespace operator with ACL rights on <child>/sys/leases/revoke|renew must still be able to revoke and renew child-namespace leases through the body-form canonical paths (request_handling.go:937-958).
Root-namespace callers must still revoke suffix-less root lease IDs; a T3 fix must reject them only for non-root requesters (expiration.go:2010-2011).

sys/revoke-prefix/<mount>/ with a trailing slash must keep revoking every lease of the requester's own namespace (expiration.go:1176-1200); mount/auth teardown uses RevokePrefix internally (mount.go:468, auth.go:274).

Same-namespace revoke and renew through every path form (sys/revoke, sys/revoke/<id>, sys/leases/revoke, sys/leases/revoke/<id>, sys/renew...) must keep working, including sync=false returning 202 (logical_system.go:2066).
Internal token revocation must keep working across namespaces (core.go:1983, request_handling.go:1173, token_store.go:1954, token_store.go:2806).

design.why: T1 is the advisory anchor: direct revoke by ID crosses namespaces and has no guard, unlike its renew sibling at expiration.go:1237. Hidden tests should also cover T3 (a suffix-less root lease revoked from a child namespace), adding a how-type shape at no extra fix site. T2 is the deepseek-type route: the single-ID branch of revoke-prefix/revoke-force looks namespace-scoped and sudo-only, so a solver is likely to dismiss it. T4 is the mimo-type coupled value: over-hardening the shared ExpirationManager breaks internal and parent-namespace revocation. T5 checks whether the guard decides on a namespace the caller supplied. Each group needs its own fix site and comes with a different reason to dismiss. If T5 cannot be shown exploitable past the ACL backstop, drop it and keep T1(+T3), T2 and T4.

unverified: The content of A's fix c0495646b41c (GHSA-v8v8-cm84-m686) is not identifiable in the pinned tree: there is no changelog entry for CVE-2026-45808 and no cross-namespace lease test. Whether A's code is present, and so whether A leaves B open, could not be checked without git history outside the read scope.
Whether B's upstream fix b20b999dd404 also covers the revoke-prefix/revoke-force single-ID branch (T2), hence the origin label uncovered_upstream.

Whether T5 is exploitable in the pinned code: the ACL is evaluated in the swapped namespace (policy/acl.go:351-373), which appears to block sibling-namespace tokens. T5's practical bypass depends on what B's advisory describes (for example, cross-namespace identity-group policies, request_handling.go:201-266).

FetchLeaseInfo's pending/irrevocable fast path keyed only by lease ID (expiration.go:1704-1712) ignores the namespace; it is only reachable through the swapped, ACL-gated sys/leases/lookup route, so it is not recorded as a trap.
The namespace of c.activeContext in core.go:1983 and ha.go:359 is assumed to be root and was not traced.
